goal:
tower-jumper: Build a polished browser game inspired by the classic vertical tower jumper genre, similar in feel to Icy Tower, but do not copy copyrighted assets, names, characters, music, logos, or exact level art. Create an original web app game with comparable core mechanics: a character runs left/right, jumps between procedurally generated platforms in an endless vertical tower, gains score from height and combos, and loses when falling below the camera.

Goal:
Create a complete, playable, production-quality web game that can be run locally and deployed as a static web app.

Preferred stack:
Use TypeScript with Vite. Use either Canvas 2D or PixiJS/Phaser if already suitable. Prefer simple, maintainable game architecture over over-engineering. The app must work on desktop browsers and have basic mobile/touch controls.

Model requirement:
Use GPT-5.5 for any asset-creation work, including visual direction, sprite concepts, generated image prompts, sound-effect planning, UI polish, animation details, particle direction, and final art-quality review. Other implementation agents may use the default model unless Orchestrate supports explicitly assigning GPT-5.5 more broadly. If Orchestrate supports per-agent model selection, assign GPT-5.5 to the Rendering/UI worker and Audio/polish worker, and use it for any verifier pass focused on art, feel, or presentation quality.

Acceptance criteria:
- npm install and npm run dev start the game.
- npm run build succeeds.
- The first screen is the actual game menu, not a marketing landing page.
- A user can start playing immediately.
- The game is fun enough to play for at least a few minutes.
- The character can climb indefinitely if skilled.
- Falling below the camera ends the run.
- Score, combo, best score, pause, restart, mute, and controls all work.
- Desktop and mobile viewport layouts are usable.
- No copyrighted Icy Tower assets, names, sprites, music, sounds, or copied UI.

Deliverables:
- Complete source code at the repository root (src/, package.json, vite config, index.html).
- Brief README with run/build instructions and controls.
- Final summary listing major files changed, verification performed, and any known limitations.

Important:
Prioritize a cohesive playable game over isolated demos. If agents make conflicting choices, reconcile toward the simplest maintainable implementation. Do not stop after scaffolding; finish the playable vertical tower jumper web app.
summary: Build the original vertical tower-jumper web game end to end (scaffold → gameplay → procgen/scoring → visuals → audio/polish → verify).

tasks.name: scaffold
tasks.scopedGoal:
Create a complete Vite + TypeScript scaffold for an original vertical tower-jumper browser game at the repository root. Do NOT name the game Icy Tower or copy any of its assets, characters, music, or UI.

Deliverables (all at repo root):
1. `package.json` declaring scripts `dev`, `build`, `preview`, `test`, and (optional) `lint`. Use `vite`, `typescript`, `vitest`. Avoid game frameworks (Phaser/PixiJS) — Canvas 2D is preferred for simplicity. Use `package-lock.json` from `npm install` and commit it.
2. `index.html` that mounts a `<canvas id="game">` plus a small loading shell. Title: "Sky Climber" (placeholder original name; downstream workers may keep or rename, but never to anything Icy-Tower-derived). Include `viewport` meta for mobile, disable double-tap zoom and pull-to-refresh on the game element.
3. `vite.config.ts` with sensible defaults (root = repo root, build target ES2020+, base = './' so the build is deployable as a static site).
4. `tsconfig.json` strict mode on, target ES2020, `moduleResolution: "bundler"`.
5. `.gitignore` covering `node_modules`, `dist`, `.DS_Store`, `coverage`.
6. `src/` modules with named exports, each a real working stub (no `throw new Error("not implemented")`; modules may render placeholder geometry but must compile and run):
   - `src/main.ts` — entry point that sets up canvas, calls into the game loop and state manager, boots into the menu state.
   - `src/config.ts` — exports a single `CONFIG` object with all tunable constants (gravity, jumpVelocity, moveAccel, friction, maxRunSpeed, terminalFallSpeed, platformMinWidth/MaxWidth, platformVerticalSpacingMin/Max, difficultyRampHeight, comboWindowMs, comboMultiplierStep, etc.) with reasonable starting values. Comment only non-obvious choices.
   - `src/loop.ts` — fixed-timestep / delta-time aware rAF loop with `start`, `stop`, and an injected `update(dtMs)` + `render(alpha)` callbacks.
   - `src/state.ts` — finite state machine for `MENU`, `PLAYING`, `PAUSED`, `GAMEOVER`, with `setState`, `getState`, and onEnter/onExit hooks.
   - `src/input.ts` — input manager exposing high-level intents (`moveLeft`, `moveRight`, `jumpPressed`, `jumpHeld`, `pauseToggle`) sourced from keyboard (Arrow/A/D, Space/W/Up, P/Escape) and a tiny touch-button API to be used by the rendering worker. Must call `preventDefault` on game keys so arrows don't scroll the page.
   - `src/player.ts` — Player struct + stub physics (just enough to render a rectangle that falls under gravity; gameplay worker will flesh out).
   - `src/platforms.ts` — Platforms manager stub: holds an array, has `update`, `render`, `reset`. Generates a few starting platforms beneath the player so the game boots without immediately falling.
   - `src/camera.ts` — vertical camera with `update(playerY)`, `transform(worldY)→screenY` helpers; never scrolls down.
   - `src/scoring.ts` — score/combo stub with `add`, `reset`, `tick`, exposing `score`, `best`, `combo`.
   - `src/audio.ts` — audio manager stub with `playJump`, `playLand`, `playCombo`, `playGameOver`, `playMenuSelect`, `setMuted`, `isMuted` — methods may be no-ops for now but signatures must be final so audio worker can wire WebAudio later.
   - `src/ui/hud.ts`, `src/ui/menu.ts`, `src/ui/gameover.ts`, `src/ui/pause.ts`, `src/ui/touch.ts` — each draws a simple legible placeholder using Canvas 2D so the menu/HUD/etc. are visible end-to-end.
   - `src/storage.ts` — `getBest()` / `setBest(n)` and `getMuted()` / `setMuted(b)` backed by `localStorage` with try/catch fallbacks to in-memory.
   - `src/render.ts` — top-level renderer that owns the canvas context, handles resize/DPR, clears, and dispatches per-state rendering to the UI modules.
7. `src/__tests__/sanity.test.ts` — at least one Vitest spec that imports `CONFIG` and asserts `gravity > 0` and `jumpVelocity < 0` (or whatever sign convention you pick — document it in `config.ts`).
8. `README.md` (overwrite the placeholder) with: project name, one-paragraph description, controls (keyboard + mobile), `npm install`, `npm run dev`, `npm run build`, `npm test`, deployment hint, originality note.

Quality bar:
- `npm install`, `npm run build`, and `npm test` must all succeed in the cloud agent VM. Run them and capture output in your handoff.
- The dev build, if started, should boot to the menu state with a visible 'Sky Climber' (or your chosen original name) heading and a 'Press Space / Tap to start' prompt. No console errors.
- Crisp rendering: handle `devicePixelRatio` so the canvas is sharp; resize listener on the window updates internal canvas size.
- All comments must explain non-obvious *why*. No narrative comments.

Non-goals for this task:
- Do NOT implement final physics, real procgen, real visuals, real audio, or final HUD polish. Downstream workers handle those. Your stubs should just keep the game compilable and render a recognisable menu.

Push exactly the orch/tower-jumper/scaffold branch and report it in your handoff.

src/ contains the listed module files, each with named exports and no `throw new Error("not implemented")`.
src/config.ts exports a single CONFIG object covering gravity, jump velocity, acceleration, friction, platform spacing, and difficulty knobs.

tasks.name: gameplay
tasks.scopedGoal:
Take the existing Vite + TypeScript scaffold (already on this branch from the scaffold task) and implement real gameplay physics, camera, collisions, and game-over.

What to build:
1. Player physics in `src/player.ts`:
   - Horizontal acceleration with friction (use CONFIG.moveAccel, CONFIG.friction, CONFIG.maxRunSpeed).
   - Gravity-based vertical motion with terminal fall speed.
   - Variable-height jump: brief upward velocity boost while jump button is still held within an early window after lift-off; tap-jumps yield short hops, held-jumps yield max-height jumps. Coyote time and jump-buffer windows for forgiving feel.
   - Horizontal screen wrapping: walking off the left edge re-enters from the right and vice versa.
   - Momentum-based jump bonus: faster horizontal speed at takeoff increases jump height (subtle multiplier; tunable in CONFIG).
   - Player state hooks: `onJump`, `onLand` callbacks the rendering/audio workers can subscribe to later.
2. Camera in `src/camera.ts`:
   - Smoothly follows the player upward; never scrolls back down once raised.
   - Tracks a `highestY` and uses easing toward target.
   - Provides `worldToScreen` and a `viewportTopY` for procgen / culling.
3. Collisions in `src/physics.ts` (new file or inside player.ts):
   - One-way platforms: only collide when the player is moving downward and the previous frame was above the platform's top.
   - Resolve to the platform top, zero vertical velocity, set `onGround = true` for one frame, fire onLand event.
4. Game-over trigger:
   - When the player's top edge falls below `camera.viewportBottomY`, the FSM transitions to GAMEOVER. The current run height (max y reached) is reported.
5. Wire up the FSM transitions:
   - From MENU, pressing jump (or tapping) starts PLAYING.
   - From PLAYING, P/Escape transitions to PAUSED; same input resumes.
   - From GAMEOVER, jump or a 'Restart' tap resets state and re-enters PLAYING.
6. Update `src/main.ts` so the running game uses the new physics and state transitions; keep the existing menu/pause/gameover placeholder UIs intact (rendering worker will polish those).
7. Tunable constants:
   - All numeric magic values must come from CONFIG. If new constants are needed, add them with reasonable starting values and brief non-obvious comments only.
8. Tests in `src/__tests__/`:
   - `physics.test.ts` — pure functions for collision (e.g. `resolveOneWay(prevTopY, nowTopY, platformTopY)`), wrapping (e.g. `wrapX(x, screenWidth)`), and momentum→jump-bonus mapping.
   - `camera.test.ts` — camera does not regress downward; `worldToScreen` is monotonic.
   - Add a smoke spec that simulates 60 frames and asserts the player rises after a held jump.

Quality bar:
- `npm install`, `npm run build`, and `npm test` must succeed.
- Run `npm run dev` if possible and confirm the player can move with arrow keys, jump with Space, wraps the screen horizontally, lands on platforms, and falling off the bottom triggers game over. Report a concise log of what you observed in your handoff.
- 60 FPS feel: integrate using delta time (dtMs / 1000) — never assume fixed frame timing.
- No narrative comments; only non-obvious *why* comments.

Do not change visuals beyond what's needed for the gameplay to be visible; rendering polish belongs to a later worker.

Push exactly the orch/tower-jumper/gameplay branch and report it in your handoff.
acceptance: Player accelerates with friction, jumps with variable height, has coyote time + jump buffer, and wraps horizontally.
Camera follows upward and never regresses; falling below it triggers GAMEOVER.
One-way platform landing is implemented and only triggers when descending onto a platform top.
FSM transitions menu→playing→paused→gameover→playing all wired with the input manager.
All physics constants live in CONFIG; no magic numbers in player/physics/camera modules.
npm run build passes; npm test passes including new physics/camera/integration specs.

tasks.name: procgen-scoring
tasks.scopedGoal:
On top of the gameplay branch, implement endless upward platform generation with a difficulty curve, the score system, the combo multiplier, and best-score persistence. Add unit tests for the pure logic.

What to build:
1. `src/platforms.ts` — production-grade procedural generator:
   - Generates platforms upward forever as the camera rises; recycles platforms whose top edge falls more than ~2 viewport heights below the camera.
   - Each platform has `{ x, y, width, kind }` where kind is `'normal' | 'small' | 'moving'`.
   - Difficulty curve based on max height climbed: smaller platform widths, larger vertical and horizontal gaps, increased moving-platform probability, with caps to keep the next platform always reachable from the previous one given CONFIG.maxRunSpeed and CONFIG.jumpVelocity (you may include a runtime assertion in dev builds and a unit test).
   - Moving platforms oscillate horizontally within a band; oscillation parameters scale with height.
   - Pure helpers (e.g. `nextPlatform(prev, rng, height) → PlatformSpec`, `isReachable(prev, next, jumpHeight, runReach) → boolean`) live in `src/procgen.ts` and are exported for testing.
   - A seeded PRNG (e.g. mulberry32) so tests are deterministic; in production seed from `Date.now()`.
2. `src/scoring.ts` — full score/combo logic:
   - Height-based score: 1 point per game unit climbed (configurable via CONFIG.heightToScore), only counted on new max heights.
   - Combo multiplier: chains of fast successive landings (within CONFIG.comboWindowMs) and/or skipped platforms (jumps that pass over more than one platform) raise the multiplier in steps; the multiplier resets on long ground time, hard landings, or wall-bumps.
   - Pure functions (`updateCombo(state, event, now) → state`, `addHeightScore(state, newHeight) → state`) exported for testing.
   - `applyMultiplier(points, multiplier)` for use elsewhere.
3. `src/storage.ts` — finalize best-score persistence:
   - `getBest()` / `setBest(n)` with try/catch around `localStorage`. Best score updates only on game-over or each new max if you prefer; document the choice.
   - Export `STORAGE_KEYS` constants.
4. HUD wiring in `src/ui/hud.ts`:
   - Show current score, best, height, and combo state (multiplier + remaining combo timer) using the placeholder visual style from scaffold/gameplay. The rendering worker will polish typography and layout — keep your implementation API-friendly so they don't need to refactor.
5. Game-over flow:
   - On entering GAMEOVER, finalize score, write best if greater, expose final stats to the gameover UI.
6. Tests in `src/__tests__/`:
   - `procgen.test.ts` — for many random seeds, verifies every consecutive (prev, next) pair is reachable per CONFIG.
   - `scoring.test.ts` — covers combo accumulation, decay, reset on hard landing, height-based score.
   - `storage.test.ts` — uses a fake localStorage to assert read/write/error fallbacks.
   - `integration.test.ts` (if practical) — simulates a series of update ticks and asserts score & combo evolve correctly.

Quality bar:
- All previous tests still pass.
- `npm run build` and `npm test` must succeed and be reflected in your handoff.
- Manually run `npm run dev` and confirm: platforms appear stretching upward, the player can climb visibly past 5+ platforms, the score and combo numbers update, dying records a best score that survives a page reload (mention you tested reload).
- All thresholds and weights live in CONFIG.

Push exactly the orch/tower-jumper/procgen-scoring branch and report it in your handoff.
acceptance: src/procgen.ts exports pure helpers used by src/platforms.ts.
Generator recycles platforms below the camera and never produces unreachable next platforms (asserted in tests).
Difficulty curve: as height grows, average platform width decreases and average gap increases, with moving platforms appearing past a threshold.
Scoring uses height + combo multiplier with reset rules; values appear in the HUD live.
Best score persists in localStorage and survives reload.
npm run build and npm test pass; new procgen/scoring/storage specs included and green.

tasks.name: rendering-ui
tasks.scopedGoal:
On top of the procgen-scoring branch, deliver the original visual identity, polished menus/HUD/pause/game-over UI, and visible mobile/touch controls. This is the visual-direction worker — think like a small-studio art lead.

Do NOT use any copyrighted Icy Tower art, character names, music, sounds, fonts, or UI motifs. Coin a fresh, clearly distinct identity (the scaffold suggests 'Sky Climber'; you may rename or evolve it, but never anywhere near 'Icy Tower'). Avoid generic placeholder-looking UI.

What to build:
1. Original visual style:
   - A tasteful pixel/arcade-inspired direction. Pick a coherent palette (commit it to a `src/theme.ts`) — e.g. neon dusk, sunset clouds, retro CRT — your choice, but consistent across menu, HUD, and game.
   - Programmatic sprites or procedurally-drawn pixel art via offscreen canvases for: the player character (idle, run, jump, fall, optional landing-squash pose), platform variants (normal, small/cracked, moving — each visually distinct and instantly readable), and decorative props (lanterns, banners, cloud shapes, parallax silhouettes).
   - Background: parallax tower interior or sky — at least two scrolling layers — that conveys vertical depth as the camera rises. Subtle altitude tinting (sky gets darker / starrier higher up) is encouraged.
   - Crisp rendering: render to a logical resolution and scale up with `imageSmoothingEnabled = false` (or DPR-aware sharp text). Keep the player and platforms instantly readable.
2. UI screens (via `src/ui/`):
   - Main menu: bold original title, version, 'Play' call to action with a key/tap hint, current best score, mute toggle, controls cheatsheet (keyboard + mobile). Animated logo or background. Looks intentional, not placeholder.
   - Pause overlay: dimmed background with 'Paused', resume hint, mute toggle, restart link.
   - Game-over: final score, height climbed, best, multiplier breakdown if available, big 'Restart' button, 'Menu' button.
   - HUD: score, best, height, combo state with a multiplier readout and a small countdown bar/ring for the combo window. Layout adapts to portrait and landscape.
3. Mobile/touch controls (`src/ui/touch.ts`):
   - Visible on touch devices and small viewports (CSS / pointer detection): big left, right, jump pads. Hold-to-jump should produce held-jump in the input manager. Buttons must not fight browser scrolling — `touch-action: none` on the canvas/buttons, prevent default on touchstart.
   - Subtle visual feedback on press.
   - Hide touch overlay on desktop unless the user starts touching.
4. Responsive layout:
   - Window resize: the canvas re-fits cleanly without cropping the player. Portrait orientation works; landscape works.
   - DPR-aware: the rendered canvas is crisp at 1x, 2x, 3x.
5. Animations:
   - Idle bob, run cycle, jump pose, fall pose, landing squash (multi-frame or shape transform).
   - Procgen platform fades in slightly when first appearing on screen (no popping).
6. Originality + asset-quality review:
   - Confirm in your handoff that no Icy Tower-derived names, sprite shapes, fonts, or UI motifs are present. Any direct visual references should be archetypes (pixel platformer, neon arcade) not the original game's specific look.
   - Capture at least one screenshot or screen recording of the playing state and the menu (commit to `assets/screenshots/` or attach via the artifacts pattern).

Quality bar:
- All previous tests still pass; add minimal smoke tests if you change pure helpers.
- `npm run build` succeeds.
- `npm run dev` looks clearly more polished and original than placeholder rectangles. Manually verify both desktop (~1280×800) and mobile (~390×844 portrait) viewports — note this in the handoff.
- No console errors or layout breaks on resize.
- No narrative comments.

Push exactly the orch/tower-jumper/rendering-ui branch and report it in your handoff.

tasks.name: audio-polish
tasks.scopedGoal:
On top of the rendering-ui branch, ship the final audio + feel polish layer: original procedural sound effects, particles, screen shake, score popups, animation polish, and the persisted mute toggle. This is the feel-and-presentation pass — think like a juice / game-feel specialist.

Do NOT use any copyrighted music or sound files. Synthesize all SFX at runtime with the WebAudio API (oscillators, noise buffers, simple envelopes). No sampled instrument loops, no third-party SFX libraries, no royalty-claim risk.

What to build:
1. Audio (`src/audio.ts`):
   - Implement: `playJump`, `playLand` (variants for soft/hard landings), `playCombo` (escalating pitch with multiplier tier), `playGameOver`, `playMenuSelect`, plus a quiet idle ambient layer (optional: a slow filtered noise pad or an arpeggio that loops; must respect mute).
   - Procedural synthesis only. Keep total CPU and memory tiny.
   - Lazy-create the AudioContext on the first user gesture (browser autoplay rules).
   - `setMuted(b)` updates a persisted localStorage flag and immediately silences/un-silences any active sources.
   - Respect the mute toggle in menu and pause overlays.
2. Particles & juice (`src/effects.ts` or similar):
   - Jump puff under the feet on takeoff.
   - Landing dust on land (scaled by impact velocity).
   - Combo sparks when the multiplier ticks up.
   - Score popups ("+125 ×3") that float upward and fade.
   - Screen shake on hard landings and on big combo tier-ups (tunable trauma → offset, decays smoothly).
3. Animation polish:
   - Landing squash (vertical scale dip, recovery via a critically-damped spring or short tween).
   - Smooth camera ease, not a hard snap.
   - Title screen subtle motion (logo bob, particles drifting in the background).
4. Game-flow polish:
   - Pause/resume is instant and pauses both physics and audio time.
   - Restart flow returns to PLAYING with reset state and no leftover effects.
   - Short, dismissible in-game control hint on the first run (e.g. 'A/D to move, Space to jump') that fades after 3 seconds or first jump. Persist 'hintSeen' in localStorage to skip it on subsequent loads.
   - Remove all debug UI (FPS counters, dev overlays). If a dev-only overlay is useful, gate it behind `import.meta.env.DEV` and verify it does NOT appear in `npm run build` output.
5. Performance:
   - 60 FPS rAF loop with delta-time physics (already from gameplay; verify it still holds with particles + audio).
   - Resize handling still correct.
6. Verify originality:
   - In your handoff confirm there is no copyrighted music, no sampled audio files, no Icy Tower-derived names anywhere.
   - Capture a short screen recording of a run with audio (or describe the audio in detail if recording with sound is not feasible) and reference it in the handoff.

Quality bar:
- All previous tests still pass; add unit tests for any new pure helpers (e.g. an envelope/decay function, a screen-shake decay function, a hint timer).
- `npm run build` succeeds.
- `npm run dev` plays smoothly on desktop and at a 390×844 mobile viewport with audio working after first interaction. Note your manual checks in the handoff.
- No console errors. No narrative comments.

Push exactly the orch/tower-jumper/audio-polish branch and report it in your handoff.
